thread:
elaine: Quick heads-up — ran the long-seq paged-hybrid benchmarks across SM90 (CUDA kernels) and SM80 (Triton kernels). Seeing a regression on SM80 vs SM90 for sequences >= 6k. Numbers below.

elaine: Benchmark snippet (model=redwood-7b, flash-paged variant, seq=8192, batch=4):
```
SM90 (cuda/fused):  tokens/s = 1180  (p95 latency 210ms)
SM80 (triton/paged-hybrid): tokens/s = 970   (p95 latency 260ms)  -> ~18% slower
KV reads/writes per token step increased ~2x on SM80 trace
Kernel occupancy lower on Triton kernels, high SMEM throttling spikes in Nsight timeline
```

elaine: Attached the perf trace link: https://perf.internal/bench/2026/1773809123 (full nvprof + nsight)

raj: Oof. Do we know if this is kernel selection (wrong variant) or runtime heuristic (batching/kv warmup)?

elaine: Initial hypothesis: Triton build picked paged-hybrid variant with smaller block size and suboptimal shared-memory tiling for sm80. Runtime batching heuristic also coalesces many short prefixes into a single batch which increases KV churn for paged backend.

chip: Can you paste the selector output for that run? The kernel mux log should show which attention variant was chosen per model/seq.

elaine: Selector log excerpt:
```
[selector] model=redwood-7b seq=8192 pool=default -> variant=paged-hybrid-triton (policy=bw_opt)
[selector] fallback=cuda-fused only if latency>SLO and capacity>0 -> not triggered
[batching] heuristic=auto (max_batch_tokens=65536, prefix_coalesce=true)
```

elaine: Also saw repeated KV page faults (runtime-level page loads) in the paged backend on SM80 which line up with the latency spikes.

raj: Two quick experiments to narrow: (1) force the cuda-fused kernel on SM80 (if available) or (2) disable prefix coalesce so batching is conservative. Can you run both?

chip: Note: forcing cuda-fused on an SM80 node may not be compiled/available — Triton build path is default for SM80 fleet. But we can cross-compile a cuda kernel for sm80 as an A/B to see pure algorithm diff. I'll try building a cuda-fused-sm80 binary.

elaine: Great. I kicked off experiment runs:
- exp/1773809123/a: prefix_coalesce=false, policy=latency_opt -> queued
- exp/1773809123/b: force_variant=cuda-fused-sm80 (cross-compiled) -> running

infra-bot: CI build for cuda-fused-sm80 (tag: sm80-cross) started (#bld-4821). Will post artifacts when done.

perf-ci: Preliminary results for exp a/b:
```
exp a (no coalesce): tokens/s = 1035 (p95 235ms)  -> better than 970 but still below SM90
exp b (cuda-fused-sm80): tokens/s = 1150 (p95 215ms) -> near parity with SM90
```

perf-ci: Full flamegraphs: https://perf.internal/bench/2026/1773809123/artefacts

elaine: So looks like two contributors: (1) batching heuristic (prefix coalesce) amplifies KV thrash on paged backend, and (2) Triton kernel variant has tiling/SMEM choices that underperform fused CUDA on SM80. Good to know.

raj: Action items:
- chip to open an issue on Triton kernel tiling for paged-hybrid (assign chip)
- eng-runtime to add a short-term runtime guard: if paged backend + prefix_coalesce + seq>4k then disable coalesce (elaine)
- infra to add cuda-fused-sm80 artifact to nightly cross-builds so we can A/B more easily (chip + infra)

chip: Filing issue: https://rb.redwood/issue/INF-2146 -> "triton: paged-hybrid tiling/SMEM tuning for sm80". Adding repro details and nsight captures.

elaine: I'll PR a small runtime guard that flips coalesce off for long seqs on paged backend (target: canary next week).

perf-ci: Note: also saw slight divergence across CUDA driver versions — sm90 runs on driver 534.x had a micro-optim vs older 520.x. Worth validating driver matrix as well.

raj: Good catch. Add driver matrix column to nightly. Also let's add a micro-benchmark that isolates KV read/write patterns (no attention compute) to prove the paging thrash hypothesis.

elaine: Will add that micro-bench. TL;DR: regression isn't a single root cause. Quick mitigations: disable aggressive coalescing for paged backend and cross-build / test cuda-fused for sm80. Longer-term: tune Triton tiled kernels for SM80.

chip: +1. If the PR lands we should canary on dedicated nodes with synthetic traffic (high prefix churn) to confirm before global rollout.

elaine: I'll schedule canary and add monitoring alerts for KV page fault rate + p95 latency delta.

infra-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary/1773809123-coalesce-guard -> https://ci.redwood/canary/1773809123 (status: pending)
